This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com
Up to 2,000 characters.

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Interactive Counter

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

content.text:
`0.html` was already in good shape, so I made six small, targeted fixes rather than a rewrite. Nothing was tested in a browser or with a screen reader, and the syntax check I tried on the inline script was blocked by the session's permissions.

## What changed

| Fix | Why |
|---|---|
| Counter no longer announces twice | The `<output>` was a live region itself, sitting next to a second live region announcing the same change. It is now `aria-live="off"`, so only "Count is now N." is read. I also dropped its `aria-label="Current count is"`. |
| Red border without an error message | `:user-invalid` could turn the email field red (type, clear, tab away) when the script had shown no message. Invalid styling now comes only from `aria-invalid`, so border and message stay in sync. |
| Input transitions respect reduced motion | The `input`/`textarea` transition was the only one outside the `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block. |
| External-link arrow fallback | Added a plain `content: "\2197"` before the alt-text version, so browsers that don't support the `/ ""` syntax still show the arrow. |
| `.visually-hidden` | Added `clip-path: inset(50%)` alongside the deprecated `clip`. |
| Script cleanup | The counter handlers now check that the display elements exist before wiring up, and the `live-message` lookup happens once instead of on every click. |

## Things I left alone

- **Author name is an email address**: both `meta name="author"` and the JSON-LD `author.name` contain `ksmith@centricle.com`. If this page is published, that's scrapeable, and a name would be more correct there.
- **CSP `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`**: a hash would be stricter, but it breaks every time the script is edited.
- **No `og:url` or canonical link**: they need the real URL, which I don't have.

## What changed

| Fix | Why |
|---|---|
| Counter no longer announces twice | The `<output>` was a live region itself, sitting next to a second live region announcing the same change. It is now `aria-live="off"`, so only "Count is now N." is read. I also dropped its `aria-label="Current count is"`. |
| Red border without an error message | `:user-invalid` could turn the email field red (type, clear, tab away) when the script had shown no message. Invalid styling now comes only from `aria-invalid`, so border and message stay in sync. |
| Input transitions respect reduced motion | The `input`/`textarea` transition was the only one outside the `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block. |
| External-link arrow fallback | Added a plain `content: "\2197"` before the alt-text version, so browsers that don't support the `/ ""` syntax still show the arrow. |
| `.visually-hidden` | Added `clip-path: inset(50%)` alongside the deprecated `clip`. |
| Script cleanup | The counter handlers now check that the display elements exist before wiring up, and the `live-message` lookup happens once instead of on every click. |

## Things I left alone

- **Author name is an email address**: both `meta name="author"` and the JSON-LD `author.name` contain `ksmith@centricle.com`. If this page is published, that's scrapeable, and a name would be more correct there.
- **CSP `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`**: a hash would be stricter, but it breaks every time the script is edited.
